title: Grateful Dead Live at Mammoth Gardens on 1970-04-24
lineage: AUD > master C-120 > reel 3.75ips > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN > WAV > SHN

ai_review.summary: Even though the tape is tinny and limited in frequency range, the performance dazzles with a soaring Dark Star, an epic The Eleven and a vibrant Easy Wind.
ai_review.review: The audience‑sourced AUD recording is noticeably thin and far‑away, but Mick's cleanup makes it tolerable enough to enjoy. Musically the show is a standout – Dark Star and The Eleven are repeatedly called “classic” or “best‑ever,” with St. Stephen, Easy Wind and Friend of the Devil also highlighted. Overall listeners rave about the intensity and rarity of the second set despite the modest sound quality.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (especially Dark Star, The Eleven and Easy Wind) while acknowledging consistent but not fatal recording flaws; the weighted average of show (≈4.5) and recording (≈3.0) yields a strong 4.2 rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as tinny, far‑away, with limited low‑end (“bottomless”) and occasional pitch fluctuations; Mick’s remaster reduces but does not eliminate these issues. MP3 compression further trims the already narrow frequency range, yet the tape remains listenable after a brief adjustment period.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers note a solid first set that improves into a spectacular second set; Dark Star segues into St. Stephen and then into an extraordinary The Eleven, with Easy Wind providing a high‑energy highlight before the show’s dramatic conclusion.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar is repeatedly praised as clear, powerful and “going OFF,” especially on Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil's bass is hard to discern in the early acoustic portion but is otherwise solid; a few reviewers mention difficulty hearing him at the start of the tape.
